Textbook contents Previous: Images · Inverse mapping, filtering and fitting Next: Deformation · from corrective shapes to a moving skeleton

Original learning chapter · updated 14 September 2026. Equations and examples explain concepts; they are not test acceptance or a support matrix.

Prerequisites: 15 · Scenes, hierarchies and packed frames, 06 · Cameras, projection and reconstructing depth, 05 · Barycentric coordinates and interpolation, 13 · Light, BRDFs and energy conservation

Separate finding a surface from lighting it

Rasterization answers which triangle occupies a pixel and where the pixel lies inside it. A geometry buffer, or G-buffer, stores that answer together with the world position, normal, texture coordinates and material identity. Shading then evaluates the selected surface. The word deferred means lighting happens after surface selection; it does not mean the calculation is postponed to another time.

A scene gives object relationships, a camera projects them, and the renderer combines their operations. Depth and a pretty colour image tell different stories: depth measures geometry along the view, while colour additionally depends on material and illumination. Keeping these channels inspectable helps diagnose an incorrect normal without blaming the camera or optimizer.

Why screen weights are not surface weights

A perspective camera divides positions by their homogeneous clip coordinate w. Interpolation in screen space therefore needs to undo that division. Let beta be the affine pixel-space barycentric weights and let w_i be the positive clip w at corner i. Corrected surface weights lambda_i divide each beta_i by its corner w_i and normalize. World position, UVs and material attributes use these corrected weights. The rasterizer's interpolated NDC depth keeps its separate definition.

Worked example: beta=(1/3,1/3,1/3) and w=(1,2,4) give unnormalized weights (1/3,1/6,1/12), whose sum is7/12. The corrected weights are(4/7,2/7,1/7). An attribute equal to(0,0,1) at the three corners is1/7 here, not the affine1/3.

Try it yourself: which corner dominates and why?

Answer: The first corner has the smallest positive w and gets weight4/7. A screen-space mixture does not correspond to an equal surface-space mixture when depths differ. With all w equal, the original beta weights are recovered.

Normal directions require care

Interpolated normals must be renormalized before material evaluation. A cube usually needs independent face normals; averaging a corner normal across its three perpendicular faces makes the cube look inflated or dented. That can be an attribute-authoring problem even when the shading formula is correct. Missing authored normals use face normals in this renderer. A zero active normal is an error rather than permission to invent a direction.

Coverage is not material opacity

Hard coverage is a discrete yes/no selection. Its local derivative with respect to geometry is zero. A soft signed-distance ramp supplies a useful local gradient, but is a declared approximation rather than physical transparency. At a candidate cutoff, a face swap or the nearest-edge boundary, smoothness is not guaranteed. The front-fragment approximation also does not promise a seamless union across every shared mesh edge. These limits must be visible beside an optimization demo.

For soft colour outside a triangle, clamping negative affine barycentrics and renormalizing provides a defined boundary extension before perspective correction. It prevents a legal black-to-white albedo from becoming negative through extrapolation. The clamp is piecewise differentiable; it does not remove the coverage approximation's discontinuities.

Filter premultiplied colour, not invisible paint

Store foreground RGB multiplied by coverage. Supersampling averages this RGB and coverage together. Otherwise invisible saturated colours can bleed into edges. For four samples consisting of one opaque red sample and three transparent ones, the mean is premultiplied RGB=(1/4,0,0), alpha=1/4. Its straight colour is red, not dark red. Over white, the composited RGB is(1,3/4,3/4).

Do not average triangle IDs, depths from unrelated surfaces, or UVs across a seam. Geometric output channels are sampled at final pixel centres even when colour and coverage are supersampled. Reconstructing colour is an image operation, not permission to reinterpret every G-buffer field as an ordinary colour channel.

A practical visibility test is an approximation too

Project a vertex, select its containing pixel, and compare its NDC depth with the raster depth using an explicit tolerance in NDC units. Behind-camera, offscreen and background probes are false. On a sloping triangle, a vertex depth can differ from the nearby pixel-centre depth even when the vertex belongs to the visible surface. This sampled test is useful but is not exact continuous visibility. Increasing tolerance changes the test and must not be hidden.

Differentiate the complete chain, within its limits

An image loss should reach mesh positions, camera intrinsics and poses, albedo maps and lighting. A material derivative alone does not prove that the full render preserves these connections. Compare analytic derivatives with two finite-difference steps away from discrete boundaries, then take a fresh small parameter step and verify the loss improves. Never detach a fitted texture or cache its parameter-dependent pyramid across optimizer steps.

Splitting an expensive shader into small calls does not bound memory if every call's backward graph remains alive. Full-image differentiation needs a measured execution strategy, such as verified recomputation, as well as finite worker and allocation limits. A preflight refusal is more honest than silently omitting gradients or claiming a large-image profile from a single shaded point.

A bounded material-recovery experiment

Hold a hard-covered head, camera, light and Classic highlight fixed, and fit only its constant RGB albedo. For each covered pixel, the independent scalar model is C=B+Sa: B is the fixed highlight, S is the diffuse coefficient and a is the fitted channel. A mean squared image loss therefore has derivative 2 times the mean of S(C-target), independently for each channel. This gives a separate analytic explanation of the gradient followed by the public renderer.

The saved64-square example takes20 fixed-rate fresh-graph steps from (0.72,0.12,0.25) toward target(0.2,0.4,0.6). Its initial mean squared error is 0.007840132184137153 and its final error is1.10225039165403e-11. The maximum parameter error is1.9497628087811192e-5. These are the saved Classic17 producer's measurements, not results of running this article. The gallery labels the initial/final images and uses the same20-times error display scale throughout.

This checks albedo recovery within fixed coverage. It does not fit every camera, material or geometric parameter, qualify large frames, or establish a consumer application's readiness. An independent material formula and a separate Decimal coverage oracle answer different questions; neither replaces the other.

Same equations, matching operations

Floating-point evaluation is an ordered calculation, not exact algebra. Two libraries can round the same elementary function differently, and a scalar divisor can take a different implementation path from a tensor divisor. When a CPU/GPU image differs, capture the same intermediate inputs before deciding which stage is responsible. Increasing an image tolerance does not repair a reference-mode byte mismatch.

The procedural scale-head check illustrates this distinction. Hard images matched, but soft masks did not. Face indices, screen weights, depths and edge distances matched exactly. A common-input comparison isolated the logistic coverage function; a second capture found a difference in the preceding division by squared blur radius. A shared sequence of exponential, division and multiplication operations repaired the exact mask comparison without changing that radius or the visibility model.

Independent high-precision values answer whether the result is accurate. Exact CPU/GPU values and first gradients answer whether device choice changes the calculation. Both checks matter. Likewise, a correctly rounded native square root can differ by one ULP from an older library reference; preserve that discrepancy and consult an independent oracle instead of declaring either library correct by name. Full-image gradient and resource tests remain necessary after a local repair.

Larger dispatches, unchanged pixel ownership

Pixels may share a material or light even when their shading calculations are independent. A larger internal dispatch can process several ordered four-point groups together without changing their equations. It keeps the same point/light pair order and fits inside the existing workspace reserve. This is different from skipping pixels, lowering precision or changing the render resolution.

The reverse pass must still combine the contributions to shared parameters. Floating-point addition depends on its order: (a+b)+c can differ from a+(b+c). The grouped renderer therefore recomputes bounded cohorts and explicitly adds their four-point contributions in reverse group order. Within a group, shared roughness and RGB fields use the same fixed adjacent-pair reduction on both devices. Independent finite differences check the derivative itself; exact CPU/GPU comparisons check the chosen calculation order.

The current boundary allows at most32 groups,128 shading points and1024 point/light pairs per internal call. It saves original inputs, releases temporary backward graphs and retains the public material's smaller admission limits. A passing small-frame batch test does not qualify a larger image's geometry, output storage or execution time. See the grouped-rendering tests for those distinct checks and the preserved reduction-order failures.

When roughness is one shared scalar,all pixels use the same material curve. The renderer prepares that curve once during forward,releases it,and prepares a fresh curve during backward. Updating roughness before a later render therefore cannot reuse stale values. A roughness map still owns independent point values and gradients. Complete input values are checked once per evaluation;each small group retains its shape,admission and native validation checks.

Memory admission uses a documented inventory of simultaneous native storage. If the largest shading cohort does not fit,the renderer selects a smaller cohort without changing its four-point gradient order. This helps scratch storage;it cannot make a full image fit when the requested output arrays alone occupy the allowance. A streamed output interface has different ownership and must be qualified separately before it can satisfy a large-frame gate.

Rejecting work while preserving pixels

The CPU rasterizer visits small pixel blocks and reuses each triangle's projected coordinates inside a block. It skips a block only when conservative bounds prove that the original rounded calculation cannot include any of its pixels. A geometric bounding box alone is insufficient: extreme or uncertain arithmetic keeps the original evaluation. Surviving pixels use the same equations and ascending face order,including depth ties and soft coverage.

Different pixels own separate fragment lists,but fitted material parameters may be shared across the image. Their gradients still require a fixed sum. The bounded streamed profile keeps each original four-point material partial and adds those partials in the original reverse order. Preparing lighting once for an admitted cohort removes repeated setup without merging those partials. Exact original-output checks,independent differences and full-job resource measurements test different parts of that claim.

These changes improve measured execution;they do not guarantee that every resolution passes the time forecast. The dashboard retains refused profiles and all earlier failures. Current scale plates show actual saved pixels and single complete-job timings,not sustained throughput or final visual acceptance.

Why the largest window can be slower

A row window and a shader group spend the same finite memory allowance. Making the window taller leaves less temporary storage for a native shader dispatch. A larger window can therefore require more, smaller dispatches. The fixed-group measurement profile reserves the existing capacity of128 points (32 ordered groups of four), then chooses the largest row window that fits it. It changes scheduling, not the physical model or any numerical tolerance.

In the fixed64-square backward fixture, the unconstrained64-row plan admits 100 points per cohort. Requiring128 points instead selects46 rows. The complete image still contains every pixel in its original camera coordinates. Shared albedo gradients retain each four-point partial and the original reverse sum.

Does independently shading each pixel make arbitrary tile-gradient sums exact?

No. Shared scene parameters receive contributions from many pixels; floating-point addition depends on order. Preserve the original partials and their reduction order, then test exact bytes and independent finite differences. The qualified streamed objective here is a global RGB mean differentiated with respect to constant albedo.

Timings from different group limits cannot be interchanged in a forecast. Both calibration and target must bind the same group capacity, wheel, helper sources, material, device and objective. Passing small controls is separate from admitting and completing a large frame. See the grouped execution checks.

Changing traversal without changing a pixel

A CPU raster window can visit rectangles first, checking every triangle in each rectangle, or visit triangles first, checking that triangle against the rectangles. Preparing the same triangle's pixel coordinates and conservative bounds once avoids repeating that setup. A fixed pixel still sees triangles in ascending order, so its depth ties and floating-point fragment calculations keep the same sequence.

This relies on separate output storage for each pixel and unchanged coverage predicates. It does not permit regrouping shared parameter gradients. The CPU path uses fixed-size scalar temporaries; it introduces no retained geometry cache or new memory allowance. Frozen original raster bytes, gradients and resource checks must pass on the newly installed wheel before any large-frame measurement counts.

Instrumentation answers where time is spent. Cold imports, nested timers and asynchronous CUDA calls can distort a small frame's apparent rate, so instrumented timings are labelled diagnostic and cannot replace the accepted forecast anchors.

Computing a narrow gradient without rebuilding its graph

The scale-measurement profile fits one constant RGB albedo. Its camera, geometry, roughness and light remain fixed during the job. The original native material already computes a full first-derivative Jacobian and vector-Jacobian product. Calling those same operations directly can remove repeated eager graph construction and engine setup without changing the derivative formula.

This requires reproducing the lighting chain rule in its original order: apply the coverage mask to the objective cotangent, then reverse the light integration factors. Keep every original four-point albedo sum and the global reverse accumulation. Do not multiply factors together early or combine groups. The original lighting forward and its checks still run, as do the complete native Jacobian and VJP. A graph-free call still pays the backward workspace allowance.

Exact partial comparisons include signed cotangents, short groups, unlit and two-sided surfaces on CPU/CUDA. Full-frame identity, independent differences, mutation/cancellation and storage tests cover separate obligations. Cold costs are included in complete-job timing; there is no prewarming or subtraction to make a forecast pass. This private profile does not qualify arbitrary losses, geometry gradients, general differentiable tiles or final scene quality.

Sharing layouts and rejecting empty regions

A constant material gives each original four-point group the same field shapes. Within one graph-free call, validate each distinct group size, then materialize the same values together. Original values are still checked across every point and the native operation still checks full derivative arithmetic. Varying fields and eager gradient graphs keep their original path. Nothing is cached across invocations.

The CPU raster can also test a large rectangle before its smaller leaves. Use the same conservative exclusion predicate: reject only a region it proves empty; otherwise split its larger extent until the unchanged pixel equations can run in small leaves. Regions partition the window, and each pixel still sees faces in ascending order. This reduces empty-region work without a new coverage rule.

The explicit traversal stack is4096 bytes inside the existing streaming reserve. Thin/wide frozen-window bytes, shared gradients and resource checks must pass on the installed artifact. These implementation changes do not themselves establish 1080p timing admission or final visual quality.

Opaque coverage: integrate the visible surface

A pixel footprint has area one in pixel units. An opaque image integrates the nearest visible surface over that footprint. A diagonal introduced only to split a square is not a translucent edge. Fading each selected triangle separately can therefore reveal the mesh even when its normals and material are smooth.

Worked example. A vertical boundary at x=1.25 covers all of pixel [0,1] and one quarter of pixel [1,2]. Their alpha values are 1 and 0.25. Moving that boundary slightly right changes only the second pixel, whose derivative is 1. A micro-edge surrogate instead distributes a boundary derivative across neighboring pixels. Matching the sum does not prove either individual derivative is correct.

Try it yourself: a triangle smaller than a pixel

A right triangle has legs 1/8 pixel and lies wholly within one pixel. What is its coverage, even if no pixel center hits it?

Answer. Its area is (1/2)(1/8)(1/8)=1/128. A center-only discovery method may report zero; that is an explicit missing contribution, not evidence that the tiny triangle has no area.

The independent development oracle uses exact rational polygon areas and affine depth comparisons. Its seven native comparison scenes distinguish image error, directional derivatives and per-window invariance. A coincident-vertex clipping bug initially discarded a derivative even though the image looked correct; the failed report is retained. Matching a second renderer or matching CPU and CUDA alone would not have established the intended pixel integral.

gffx boundary. These are constant-face-colour, small-scene C11 research candidates. They do not install an opaque renderer or qualify arbitrary shading, CUDA, streamed reverse accumulation or final showcase quality. Broad soft visibility remains a separate fitting aid. See the independent checks and the image and gradient comparison.

From the reference to a native alpha primitive

The next experimental implementation integrates the union of projected triangles in native C on the CPU. Union coverage removes artificial shared-edge fading and includes triangles too small to hit a pixel center. Its first reverse derivative accumulates the clipped-area derivatives in a fixed order. Independent rational areas, nonuniform pixel weights, finite differences and window boundaries check different parts of that claim; a single attractive image cannot replace them.

The explicit coverage='opaque' scene route currently returns only the mask. It does not yet integrate depth-ordered shaded colour. Float32 and float64 are supported on the CPU; CUDA and higher derivatives are refused. A bounded scratch buffer and explicit candidate-capacity refusal prevent silently dropping geometry. This small-scene reference path has no large-frame throughput claim.

Scene projection has its own failure modes. A triangle crossing the camera plane can have misleading divided depths. A retained failing test shows why front/behind classification must happen before rejecting a distant triangle. Partial clipping is explicitly unsupported rather than returning a misleading empty mask. The legacy hard and broad soft paths remain separately tested.

Global image coordinates introduce another trap: subtracting large polygon areas can erase a small triangle. A retained test lost an exactly representable area of 1/32768 after translating it far from the origin. Evaluate clipping and area in coordinates local to each pixel, keeping the geometry derivatives and global candidate discovery. Exact translated-area and gradient controls then guard this case without clamping small contributions or loosening accuracy limits.

gffx boundary: what M1 does not promise

This is an eager composition, not a path tracer or a new native renderer. There is no automatic global illumination, shadowing, display conversion, physical transparency or fully qualified near-plane clipping. SH irradiance has a labelled diffuse path; it is not full glossy environment lighting. Numerical tests, exact device parity, resource measurements, visual review and consumer fitting each have their own acceptance gate. A beautiful image closes none of them by itself.

Material transitions: integrate every visible region

Opaque coverage belongs to the union of visible surfaces, not to separate triangle opacities. A material jump changes radiance at its interface; moving that interface contributes the radiance difference times its swept area. A continuous bilinear texture instead has cell boundaries where its derivatives change.

Perspective UV and roughness thresholds become homogeneous affine lines in a screen triangle. Split visible polygons at those lines before integration. Native quadrature now emits face identity, screen barycentrics and area weights; the scene then evaluates perspective attributes and full nonlinear Principled shading at the nodes. Its reverse pass transports both node positions and integration weights.

The independent material reference uses exact moving partitions, outward-rounded mixed derivatives, and a centred Taylor envelope with a seventh-order remainder for the tested roughness interval. Image and first-gradient errors are enclosed separately. A thin-feature negative control prevents a sampled zero from becoming proof, and uncertain limiter branches refuse instead of picking a midpoint.

The scene composition is an explicit bounded CPU/CUDA float64 Principled/directional profile with bilinear level-zero albedo and clamp/repeat addressing. Fixed native Gauss5 geometry is not a universal error certificate: arbitrary branch crossings, horizons, dense workloads and the final showcase still need gates. Small streamed windows and device conformance have separate finite qualification. Integration bounds, native floating rounding and physical loss-table approximation are three different claims.

Moving visibility: differentiate the region and the material

A moving silhouette changes which part of a pixel sees the object. With a vertical boundary at t and foreground to its right, the pixel derivative is minus the foreground radiance at t. At a depth intersection, moving the boundary exchanges surfaces: the derivative is the left radiance minus the right radiance. Freezing visibility would lose these terms even if shading gradients were correct.

The reference now transports the exact visible polygons and their integration Jacobians together with the shading field. Perspective attributes attached to a moving triangle subtract its interpolated screen velocity before evaluating the field tangent. An entirely visible translated material must not acquire a false colour change merely because its screen coordinates changed.

Exact polynomial predicates certify a local interval in which visibility keeps its combinatorial structure. A zero predicate is accepted only if it is identically zero; a quadratic change invisible to a first-order test is refused. The two nonlinear fixtures have a certified geometry interval of plus/minus 1/1024.

Sixteen exact controls and five nonlinear/installed-wheel checks pass. Independent 90-digit boundary formulas lie inside the gradient enclosures. A different Gauss16 integral using installed shader calls and autodiff agrees within the existing floating-point tolerances. Its rounding can exceed the much tighter quadrature interval; the integration bound does not certify native rounding. General topology transitions, material knots, varying roughness/textures, production nonlinear scene colour, CUDA and final showcase acceptance remain open.

Nonlinear shading: an error interval for the actual pixel

Shading at triangle corners and interpolating their colours changes a nonlinear Principled image. The reference instead interpolates the surface attributes with perspective correction, evaluates the complete material, and integrates radiance over each exact frontmost region of the pixel.

A sample-grid comparison can miss a narrow feature on both grids. Our bounded reference uses outward-rounded arithmetic and a Gauss remainder derived from interval bounds on spatial derivatives. RGB and the chosen parameter tangent get separate error intervals. Polynomials that vanish at every coarse quadrature node are deliberate negative controls: their positive integrals must not become zero.

The first smooth, fixed-roughness pixel passed with 44 accepted cells from 87 examined. Its RGB interval radii are at most 1.185e-13, and the tested normal/albedo tangent radii at most 2.987e-14, inside the unchanged 1e-12 reference budget. The installed shader evaluated at 1100 weighted points agrees inside all six intervals. This comparison is not the source of the error bound.

The bound concerns integration of the stored material-resource model, not its physical-table approximation error. Spatially varying roughness, texture cells, interpolation-knot and horizon partitioning, moving visibility, full scene colour, CUDA and final showcase acceptance remain open. Failed depth/time-limit attempts are retained. Unresolved work refuses a result; it never returns a last estimate.

Visible colour: integrate after resolving depth

The CPU opaque_integrate primitive integrates a declared screen-affine RGB field over the nearest visible polygon pieces of each pixel. It returns premultiplied RGB and covered area; a constant background is added as RGB + (1-alpha) background. Shared edges between triangles representing the same affine field do not introduce transparency. A depth intersection can create an interior visibility boundary even when no triangle edge crosses a pixel.

The independent Fraction reference integrates each convex piece by exact triangle-fan centroid quadrature; native C uses polygon first moments. Image agreement, geometry/depth derivatives and corner-radiance derivatives are checked separately. The existing float64 1e-12 and float32 1e-6 oracle bounds remain fixed.

This stage does not approximate a nonlinear Principled shader by calling it at vertices. The bounded smooth-pixel reference above begins nonlinear and perspective-varying radiance qualification; complete scene integration and derivatives remain open. The current CPU candidate cap is32; overflow is an explicit refusal. CUDA, dense-scene throughput and final shaded showcase acceptance remain open.

Bounded windows: one image, one ordered derivative

Opaque colour windows keep the original camera coordinates and resolve every pixel's visible surfaces. The optional opaque_tile_pixels caps window width; the planner chooses a fitting width automatically when it is omitted. Outputs, cotangents, input adjoints and temporary work still count against64MiB. A window cannot make an oversized retained output disappear.

Backward saves inputs and recomputes one pixel at a time in a fixed order, independent of the forward window width. This avoids retaining every window's shading graph and keeps accumulation predictable. The initial CPU/CUDA scene comparison exposed differing three-term perspective sums; explicit normalization and its VJP repaired it. The failed report remains visible.

Independent piecewise-constant pixel tests now include roughness0.15 through0.95, metallic and dielectric endpoints, two-sided orientation and unlit surfaces. Exact region motion supplies the interface gradient. A region whose interval crosses an unresolved horizon or angular knot is refused, not assigned a sampled branch. These finite fixtures and the small CUDA windows are engineering evidence; they do not yet establish the original mesh or the final SIGGRAPH-quality showcase.

Returning to the original mesh: admission is not accuracy

The original 5,002-vertex, 10,000-triangle fixture has constant roughness 1, F0 0.04 and albedo (0.2, 0.4, 0.6). Conservative projected-box counts stay below the 32-face cap: maxima are 30 at 128 square, 20 at 256 square, and 18 at both 512 square and 1080p. These counts establish candidate capacity only; they do not establish visible-piece capacity, nonlinear accuracy or frame time.

At 1080p the retained output/cotangent reserve alone is 200,179,712 bytes, above the unchanged 64 MiB allowance. Smaller temporary tiles cannot remove retained full-frame storage. No full original-mesh opaque frame is admitted.

Original pixel (160,128) in the 256-square camera exposed a reference problem: angular-table knots break the smoothness assumption of a derivative remainder. The new reference freezes a smooth cubic extension per integration cell, then adds an outward enclosure of the actual piecewise expression minus that extension. A separate mean-value cosine bound reduces interval dependency. Neither a midpoint branch nor agreement between sample grids is an error certificate.

Image and angle-independent material derivatives are separate obligations. Moving-angle and horizon crossings still require qualification. Cell, depth, time and numerical limits are unchanged; incomplete attempts remain explicit refusals in the preserved reports. This is engineering evidence on the path to the requested SIGGRAPH-quality demonstration, not showcase acceptance.

The first original pixel is now independently certified: two visible triangles, 128 examined cells and 65 accepted leaves provide separate RGB and albedo-tangent radii below 1e-12. Installed CPU and CUDA values lie inside those enclosures; their RGB, mask and full albedo Jacobian bytes also agree. This is one pixel with fixed geometry, not a whole image or a moving-angle gradient certificate.

Moving knots and horizons: the missing boundary term

Changing geometry or view direction moves the angular-table boundary through an integration region. The reference now adds the ordinary piecewise derivative and a separate conservative jump-transport bound. It certifies a crossing only when a spatial derivative has fixed sign throughout the cell; uncertain tangencies refuse. One real-resource knot and rigid geometry motion pass independent bounds on CPU and CUDA. This does not certify every moving scene.

At a view horizon,pointwise differentiation can miss a radiance jump entirely. The analytical test gives a positive unpartitioned gradient of0.042997,while the correct pixel gradient is negative,-0.109973. An explicit moving horizon cut recovers the boundary contribution and passes on both devices. A light-horizon case is checked separately. General production horizons remain open: varying normals and view directions can make the boundary curved.

Full-frame storage is not full-frame speed

The internal-disk development store preserves RGB,mask and their cotangents, rejects incomplete frames and checks every block before replay. A1080p synthetic frame uses132710400 disk bytes with at most32768 payload bytes per block. A real3x3 textured scene preserves each device's resident pixels and ordered vertex gradient exactly. Neither result is a1080p render timing.

The original32/64-square startup frames have maximum candidate counts68/44, above the unchanged32-face cap. No complete matching opaque timing anchors exist, so a full-frame forecast is refused. Old hard/soft timings and one-pixel crops cannot qualify this new execution profile. Production horizon integration, external-storage wiring and a bounded complete-frame cost path remain required before the original mesh and final SIGGRAPH-quality demonstration are admitted.

Production horizons, exact arithmetic and host-owned windows

The production opaque scene now inserts linear horizon cuts. Constant or uniform normals give a linear view boundary; directional lighting gives a linear light boundary. A varying normal dotted with a varying view can be quadratic. Conservative coefficient signs can exclude a crossing; unresolved curved and grazing boundaries refuse. The shared cut limit and numerical criteria stay.

An off-centre3x3 camera exposed a scalar-division rounding difference before shading. Tensor dimension division and an explicit RGB coverage-weight VJP restore all captured CPU/CUDA stage and final-gradient bytes. The smaller knot case separately needs fixed caller broadcast/channel/sample reduction order. Exact agreement is checked independently from the reference error bounds.

The public opaque_window operation uses the original camera coordinates and reserves only the requested rectangle, plus inputs, cut/horizon storage and scratch. A host driver writes complete ordered internal files and replays one pixel at a time. Input mutation, cancellation and corruption refuse. File I/O and scheduling remain outside the renderer. Finite complete-frame reports name their actual scene and resolution; they never stand in for the original mesh or the requested final SIGGRAPH-quality demonstration.

Following a curved view horizon

The opaque61 checkpoint below established the independent reference; the following native section records its implementation.

The original mesh has174 retained faces whose normal/view dot product changes sign. Because both interpolated vectors vary, their homogeneous dot product is quadratic. A straight cut generally changes the forward integral and its gradient. The independent reference now follows a certified curved boundary on one visible triangle. It maps the curved region to a square and differentiates both the mapping and its area weight. That preserves the boundary contribution which a pointwise shading derivative would miss.

Exact polynomial signs certify one transverse crossing along each radial ray. Tangencies and unsupported topologies refuse. Closed parabolic coverage and moving-triangle formulas test the reference separately. Direct radial composition of perspective fields avoids interval cancellation on a thin triangle without relaxing accuracy. The real selected patch passes in8 cells with image and motion radii below1e-12; the earlier90-second refusal remains historical evidence.

This uses actual original geometry with a declared roughness1,F0=1,albedo0 control material. Full original material integration,shared native CPU/CUDA curved quadrature and complete-frame admission remain open. The new diagram explains this gate; it is not a replacement for the requested final rendered showcase.

Native curves: images,gradients and complete frames

The shared native CPU/CUDA path now follows the conic root and differentiates both sample locations and area weights. Linear cuts keep their existing path. A strict topology guard is separate from a shader integration-error bound; unsupported tangencies and over-cap pixels still refuse.

The first native curved pixel had an accurate image but an inaccurate gradient. Two angular strips per side repaired that pixel,then a2-by-2 frame exposed a larger gradient error after clipping. Four strips per side consume eight of the existing32 pieces and200 of800 nodes. Neither the numerical tolerance nor the memory allowance was raised. These failures remain visible in the test history.

Complete-pixel RGB and normal motion are checked against an independent outward reference. CPU/CUDA bytes,host-storage replay,frame-integral accuracy and complete execution timing are separate gates. The tests name their small control scene and resolution. Actual original-mesh full-material integration and the requested final SIGGRAPH-quality demonstration are still required for M1.

The original material: execution and accuracy are separate

The complete silhouette pixel now evaluates every visible piece using the original blue material,F0=.04 and roughness1. A compact angular quadrature rule uses120 nodes per crossed fan instead of200,while keeping the800-node ceiling. Constant material bindings also allow the planner to reserve fewer impossible cut arrays; unknown material-cut profiles retain the conservative reservation. The initial full-pixel memory and capacity failures remain in the test history.

CPU and CUDA produce identical colour,mask and albedo-Jacobian bytes for this pixel. Their agreement does not establish the correct integral. The independent reference has to follow the actual piecewise angular-loss table as well as the curved visibility boundary. Its current residual bounds exhaust256 cells on the first visible piece. Neither accuracy nor the work budget was relaxed.

This leaves complete original-frame qualification and the final SIGGRAPH showcase open. The next numerical work is a tighter certified treatment of angular joins,including boundary transport for moving-angle gradients. A small successful control image is not the requested final original-mesh demonstration.

Certifying one piece does not certify the pixel

The next reference integrates the signed correction around angular lookup boundaries and bounds its remaining error. A Peano kernel measures how a quadrature rule responds to changes in the integrand. Here the bound includes ordinary third derivatives and explicit jumps in value,slope and curvature. It never assumes that stored binary knots join perfectly. Polynomial convex hulls provide the kernel bounds; sampled maxima are not certificates.

Exact rational dot products reduce repeated-normalization uncertainty without changing the shading formula. Closed-form tests check the correction,its spatial derivatives,box scaling and refusal of unsupported moving-angle tangents. The checker now propagates an external deadline immediately; its earlier subdivision retry is retained as a failed regression.

This certifies the first of13 exact visible pieces of the original blue-material pixel. Installed CPU and CUDA shading and albedo derivatives agree with that piece's independent interval. The whole-pixel experiment still reaches its shared90-second deadline on the second piece,so there is no whole-pixel pass. Continuing each piece with a fresh timer would not satisfy this test.

The remaining work needs a more efficient partition that follows the angular boundaries while retaining the same error and work limits. Complete original frames and the final SIGGRAPH-quality showcase remain open. The earlier gallery continues to show finite engineering evidence,not a completed showcase.

Bounding an approximate partition

An affine classifier L may approximate a nonlinear cosine q while retaining a rigorous bound |q-L| at most delta. If their branch choices disagree at knot k, the point lies inside |L-k| at most delta and |q-k| at most delta. Rational clipping gives the area of that band.
